identity.title: MYC primes a paralog synthetic lethality involving the mitochondrial translocase subunits TIMM17A and TIMM17B and N-Acetylaspartate.

content.abstract: To identify the genes and pathways required for the survival of MYC-amplified cancers, we engineered an isogenic cell system in which transformation is driven by oncogenic MYC. Using a genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 library, we identified the mitochondrial membrane translocase TIMM17A as uniquely essential for the survival of MYC-transformed cells. This dependency arises from MYC-driven suppression of TIMM17B, the paralog of TIMM17A. TIMM17A/B is an essential component of the TIM23 mitochondrial protein import complex, and the MYC-induced suppression of TIMM17B creates a strong dependency on TIMM17A. N-acetylaspartate supplementation rescued TIMM17A dependency in MYC-amplified cell lines, highlighting the unique and crucial role of this metabolite in the cell fitness of MYC-amplified cancers. These observations identify a paralog dependency required for the survival of a subset of MYC-driven cancers.
